rounds.proof_sketch: With fixed shape [128, 4000] and dim=1: outer_size=128, dim_size=4000, inner_size=1. block_size_dim=min(256, inner_size)=min(256,1)=1, yielding a (1,1,1) thread block. Thus threadIdx.x=0 and threadIdx.z=0 for all threads. The mutation threadIdx.x→threadIdx.z produces identical loop iteration: for(inner_idx=0; 0<1; inner_idx+=1) in both cases.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation replaces threadIdx.x with threadIdx.z in the loop initializer. Under the fixed configuration with dim=1 on a [128, 4000] tensor, inner_size equals 1 (product of dimensions after dim=1, which is empty). The block_size_dim is computed as min(256, inner_size)=min(256,1)=1. When dim3 is constructed with a single value, it creates a (1,1,1) block, meaning blockDim.x=blockDim.y=blockDim.z=1 and threadIdx.x=threadIdx.y=threadIdx.z=0 for the single thread. Both original and mutant iterate the loop identically: starting at 0, checking 0<1 (true), processing inner_idx=0, then incrementing to 1 and exiting. The mutation would only be detectable with inner_size>1 (requiring dim=0), but dim is a fixed model parameter.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation only manifests when inner_size>1, which requires dim=0 for this tensor shape. Since dim is fixed at 1 during model initialization (not a tensor input), no value-level test can expose the difference. The kernel launches with 1-thread blocks where threadIdx.x=threadIdx.z=0.
rounds.recommendations: When testing GPU kernels with configurable dimension parameters, mutation testing should also vary the dimension parameter across valid ranges, not just tensor values. This mutation would be immediately killed by testing with dim=0 where inner_size=4000 would expose the threadIdx indexing bug through race conditions or missing coverage of inner positions.
